headline: Super Mario Sunshine joins Nintendo Switch Online's GameCube library next month
summary: The divisive 2002 platformer, featuring the plumber and a sentient water cannon, arrives on NSO on August 13th.
details: Nintendo is finally adding Super Mario Sunshine to its Nintendo Switch Online GameCube library next month. The 2002 title, which followed Super Mario 64, was one of the first games announced for the GameCube Classics app but is only now being released.

In the game, Mario visits the tropical Isle Delfino for a vacation, only to be framed for vandalism by a shadow version of himself. He must then clean up the mess with the help of a water-spewing device called FLUDD, all while dealing with an obligatory princess-saving mission.

Super Mario Sunshine is known for its unique gameplay mechanics centered around FLUDD, but it's also considered one of the more divisive 3D Mario games due to its physics, controls, and camera, which some critics found to be less refined than expected from Nintendo.

Its arrival on NSO is significant as it means all home console 3D Mario games are now playable on the Switch. The game was previously available in the 2020 Super Mario 3D All-Stars collection but has since been delisted.

As an emulated version of the GameCube original, Super Mario Sunshine on NSO will retain its 2002 characteristics, including its challenges, but will feature upscaled visuals and built-in save states. It will be available starting August 13th.

headline_marked: [[Streaming QR codes]] at 60 FPS achieves nearly 190 KB/s data rate
headline: Streaming QR codes at 60 FPS achieves nearly 190 KB/s data rate
summary: This browser-based method requires no app, networking, or pairing, only camera access.
details: A new method allows for streaming QR codes at 60 frames per second, achieving a data rate of nearly 190 KB/s. This technique enables phone-to-phone data transfer without the need for dedicated apps, network connections, or device pairing.

The system relies solely on camera access to capture and decode the QR code stream. This innovative approach bypasses traditional data transfer methods, offering a unique solution for quick and accessible file sharing between devices.

The browser-based implementation means users can initiate transfers directly from a web page, making it highly convenient. The only permission required is access to the device's camera, simplifying the setup process significantly.

This method is particularly useful for transferring small to medium-sized files quickly and efficiently. The high frame rate and data throughput demonstrated in tests suggest a promising future for QR code-based data transmission.
